zero_init_dead_point.explanation: run 1 with the bilin18 zero-init write convention: the quadratic routing coefficient has zero gradient at write=0, so all writes stayed exactly zero for 4122 steps; V2/V3/V4 are bigram readouts of the embedding, V7 is the uniform predictor log(50257)=10.8249. Checkpoints archived as qk_deeproute_V*_deadinit.pt.

verdict.headline: Only V5 (subspace partitioning) is within the 0.05-nat budget (+0.0459 +/- 0.0032 seq-clustered). Weight-readable wiring: V5 support score Spearman ~0 overall (0.29 on the 89 causally-effectual pairs; top-4 causal pairs at 97th-99th support percentile) -- readable in principle, but training gives no localization pressure. V7 combo gets the best weight-causal agreement (0.50 overall, 0.74 on effectual pairs) and extreme routing sparsity (1.23 effective inputs) but costs +0.51 nats and leaves 7 of 12 blocks causally dead. V3 pure-TN squared routing gives near-one-hot depth wiring (k95=1 at block 6 with 0.999 causal recovery) at +0.33 nats. Discovery: quadratic routing coefficients have zero gradient at write=0, so the bilin18 zero-init convention is a dead fixed point for V2/V3/V4/V7; fixed with std 0.004 write init. Recommendation: advance V5 to the level-5 pass; retrain suggestion for bilin18: V5 projections + V6 static dilation mask (both structural, near-free) plus group-sparsity on input-weight support to make the wiring actually read off the weights; avoid learned multiplicative routing at this scale.
